mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment and housing starts indicates robust consumer demand and confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through stronger corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market expansion regime characterized by rising housing starts, S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 20 trading days due to increased construction activity and consumer spending spillovers.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of housing expansion periods, or the Rank IC for HOUST in housing boom regimes is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may prompt monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicates a monetary tightening cycle coinciding with labor market weakness, which depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 6.5%), S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit pressures.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE in high unemployment regimes is below 0.02.
